<div id="content">
<div class="sect1">
<h2 id="_overview"><a class="link" href="#_overview">1. Overview</a></h2>
<div class="sectionbody">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This document describes installation steps before operating LENA Server on a typical VM Host environment. For the complete features and operational guidance of LENA, refer to the separately provided Administrator Manual.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This document is based on LENA version 1.3.3 and includes the following:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>LENA installation</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Linux-based</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Windows-based</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_components"><a class="link" href="#_components">1.1. Components</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>LENA consists of a Web Server, a WAS (Web Application Server), a Session Server, a Node Agent that monitors and controls the status of Web Servers, an Advertiser installed on Application Servers that provides status information, and the Manager, an integrated management tool for administrators.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_server"><a class="link" href="#_server">1.1.1. Server</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>LENA provides three types of servers: Web Server, Application Server, and Session Server. Their roles are as follows:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Web Server: Provides web resources based on user requests. It acts as the front for application services provided by the Application Server and can optionally provide load balancing and a security layer (SSL).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Application Server: Runs and serves applications written in Java.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Session Server: Maintains user sessions across Application Servers.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_agent_advertiser"><a class="link" href="#_agent_advertiser">1.1.2. Agent, Advertiser</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Agents are installed on Nodes and Servers and are responsible for control and monitoring.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Node Agent</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Aggregates Web Server status monitoring data and provides it to the Manager.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Advertiser</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Aggregates Application Server status monitoring data and provides it to the Manager.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_manager"><a class="link" href="#_manager">1.1.3. Manager</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Manager is a web application that provides control and monitoring of Nodes and Servers through the Node Agent and Advertiser. Representative features include the following.</p>
</div>

<tr>

</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Server Cluster</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">

</li>

</li>

</li>
<li>
<p>Snapshot for backup/restore of Server Cluster configuration</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Graceful restart of Servers registered in a Server Cluster</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Resource</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="ulist">

Database / DataSource / MessageService(JMS) / Transaction(JTA) / Application / LoadBalancer(SLB)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>View and register/modify/delete the list of servers using a resource</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>

<tr>

</li>

</li>

</li>

</li>

</li>
</ul>
</div></div></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_mechanism"><a class="link" href="#_mechanism">1.2. Mechanism</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>LENA provides monitoring and centralized management of Web Servers and WAS through the Manager. To enable this, an Agent is installed per Node, called the Node Agent. The Node Agent receives user commands from the Manager to control the Web Server/WAS installed on the Node, and sends monitoring information for the host/VM where the Node is installed and for the Web Server back to the Manager.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock text-center">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/1_2_mechanism.png" alt="FullyContainer" width="623" height="471">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 1. LENA Manager monitoring and centralized management workflow</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In addition to LENA Manager, Web Server, and WAS, components such as the Manager Repository used for Manager operations, the Session Server for session clustering, and the Advertiser for collecting WAS monitoring information enable monitoring and centralized management via the Manager.</p>
</div>

<div class="sect1">
<h2 id="_installation_prerequisite"><a class="link" href="#_installation_prerequisite">2. Installation Prerequisite</a></h2>
<div class="sectionbody">
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_system_requirements"><a class="link" href="#_system_requirements">2.1. System Requirements</a></h3>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_hardware_resource"><a class="link" href="#_hardware_resource">2.1.1. Hardware Resource</a></h4>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>CPU</strong><br>
This entirely depends on how much performance the Web Application you want to run requires. For basic LENA service operation, we recommend 2 cores or more.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Memory</strong><br>
For Memory, refer to the table below. All modules except Web Server operate on JVM basis and use Heap Memory. LENA has pre-configured default Heap Memory values, which are installed with these values during installation but can be modified as needed. For stable operation, ensure that the sum of Heap Memory settings for all modules installed on one physical server does not exceed the remaining memory capacity of the physical server.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The minimum requirements for installing LENA Manager and each Server are as follows:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 20%;">
<col style="width: 20%;">
<col style="width: 20%;">
<col style="width: 20%;">

</colgroup>

</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session Server</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">JDK 1.8 +</p></td>

<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">512 MB</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">1 GB</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Each Server is installed based on default Memory settings during installation, and Memory settings can be changed and applied above the minimum Memory requirements.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_operating_system"><a class="link" href="#_operating_system">2.1.2. Operating System</a></h4>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Linux</strong><br>
Supports Redhat (RHEL, CentOS) 6.5 or higher / Ubuntu 12.04 or higher and is the most recommended operating system. To match the characteristics of general x86 architecture, we recommend distributed installation on multiple low-capacity servers rather than large-capacity integrated server configuration.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Windows</strong><br>
Supports Windows 7 or higher. Unlike Linux/Unix, due to Windows characteristics, it provides Windows Service registration functionality to run LENA Module in the background. Otherwise, LENA Module always runs in the foreground.<br></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Linux/Unix basically provides scripts to run LENA Module.<br>
If registration as OS Service is required, the server administrator must directly configure it according to the OS environment.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Unix</strong><br>
Supports Solaris, HP-UX, and AIX. Unlike Linux/Windows, Unix does not provide new versions and patches by default, and when needed, they are created and distributed through individual review by OS version, which typically requires about 2 weeks.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_account"><a class="link" href="#_account">2.1.3. Account</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Before installing LENA, an account is needed for LENA installation and startup. Unless there is a suitable reason, Root / Administrator accounts are not recommended for security reasons and cannot be used to run LENA, so create a separate account in advance.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock warning">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-warning" title="Warning"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
Although not recommended in X86 architecture, suppose multiple different business systems are operated on one physical server, and the responsible operators are separated by system, and accounts are separated for access control between systems. In this case, Node should be installed/configured and operated by operator account (by business system), and it is recommended to configure LENA Manager by system as well.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_directory"><a class="link" href="#_directory">2.1.4. Directory</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Before proceeding with LENA installation, you must prepare an installation directory that can be used by the account created in the previous step. The table below is the directory structure suggested by LENA, and you can use a directory structure that matches your policy.
The table below is explained based on Linux/Unix, but for Windows, configure the directories identically under C:.</p>
</div>

<div class="paragraph">
<p>The consideration is whether to separate log files. If not separately configured, logs are created by default under the path where LENA Node is installed. To make log checking easier and disk capacity management convenient, we recommend separating the log directory.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If possible, we recommend mounting separate external disk volumes to Node, log, and source directories to isolate them from the OS System area.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_network"><a class="link" href="#_network">2.1.6. Network</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The diagram below shows the traffic flow between each LENA Module. LENA Management-related paths and Web Service-related paths are expressed in detail.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock text-center">

<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/2_1_6_prerequisite_network_traffic.png" alt="FullyContainer" width="623" height="471">
</div>

</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The traffic paths between LENA modules and the ports used as shown in the above diagram are as follows. The specified port numbers are predefined defaults and can be specified separately when installing each module. After selecting ports by referring to the table below, the firewall must be opened in advance.</p>

<p>The ports used by LENA use ports above 1025 for security requirements. However, if you need to use well-known ports such as port 80 when providing services, refer to the port 80 usage guide provided in the appendix.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>

<div class="sect1">
<h2 id="_installation"><a class="link" href="#_installation">3. Installation</a></h2>
<div class="sectionbody">
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_lena_installation"><a class="link" href="#_lena_installation">3.1. LENA Installation</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Upload the LENA installation file to a prepared directory on the target server. Using the installation file, install LENA Manager on the server intended for the Manager, install the Web Server Node on the server intended for the Web Server, and install the WAS Node on the server intended for WAS.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Before proceeding with the LENA installation, refer to the JVM section of the Operator Manual and install the JDK in advance.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After installing the Node, install the Web Server and WAS through the LENA Manager Web UI. The LENA installation files are categorized as follows by product edition and purpose.</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<caption class="title">Table 5. LENA installation file classification (OS: Linux/Windows 64bit / LENA: as of 1.3.3.0)</caption>
<colgroup>

<col style="width: 16.6668%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>

<div class="paragraph">
<p>For the differences between the Enterprise Edition and the Standard Edition, refer to the Server Module section of the Operator Manual.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>LENA installation on Linux and Windows proceeds in the same overall manner.
This document explains based on Linux.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_lena_manager_installationexecution"><a class="link" href="#_lena_manager_installationexecution">3.1.1. LENA Manager Installation/Execution</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The LENA installation package is provided as a compressed file; upload it to the server to be installed and extract it before use. LENA Manager is included in the WAS Node installation file. Upload the installation file to the path where you will install (e.g., /engn001/lena) and extract it.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>LENA Manager is included in the WAS Node installation file.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Verify installation path and uploaded installation file</dt>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash"> [lena]# cd /engn001/lena
 [lena]# ll
 -rw-rw-r-- 1 lena lena lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock tip">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-tip" title="Tip"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When extracting, a directory is created using the filename excluding the extension.<br>
Rename this directory to the simplified name 1.3 and use it.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Extract the installation file / Rename directory</dt>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash"> [lena]# tar -xvzf lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz
 [lena]# mv lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0 1.3
 [lena]# ll
 drwxr-xr-x 12 lena lena 1.3
 -rw-rw-r-- 1 lena lena lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Use the install.sh file (e.g., /engn001/lena/1.3/bin/install.sh) for installation.<br>
Install using the following commands.</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">LENA Manager installation</dt>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">[lena]# cd /engn001/lena/1.3/bin
[lena]# ./install.sh create lena-manager
*******************************
* LENA Server Install ! *
*******************************
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| 1. SERVICE_PORT is the port number used by Manager.
| ex : 7700
| 2. MONITORING_PORT is the port number used by Manager for monitoring.
| ex : 16100
| 3. RUN_USER is user running LENA Manager.
| ex : lena, wasadm
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Input SERVICE_PORT for execution. (q:quit)
Default value is '7700'
7700</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After LENA Manager installation completes, script files related to LENA Manager are generated in the directory where install.sh was executed.</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<caption class="title">Table 6. LENA Manager management scripts</caption>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33.3333%;">
<col style="width: 66.6667%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Script Name</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">start-manager.sh</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Starts LENA Manager.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">ps-manager.sh</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Checks whether LENA Manager is running.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">stop-manager.sh</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Stops LENA Manager.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Run start-manager.sh to start LENA Manager.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">[lena]# ./start-manager.sh
--------------------------------
 LENA Manager
--------------------------------
Using LENA_HOME : /engn001/lena/jadeu3/1.3
Using JRE_HOME : /engn001/java/jdk1.8.0_202
Using SERVER_PID : /engn001/lena/jadeu3/1.3/modules/lena-manager/lena-manager_solmanager.pid
Using SERVER_HOME : /engn001/lena/jadeu3/1.3/modules/lena-manager
Using SERVER_ID : lena-manager
Using INSTANCE_NAME : lena-manager_solmanager
LENA started.</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once LENA Manager starts normally, you can access the Manager via the server’s Service Port.<br>
<a href="http://Server_IP:7700" class="bare">http://Server_IP:7700</a></p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_1_manager_access.png" alt="3 1 1 manager access">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 3. LENA access screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Log in with the following initial account/password to see the initial screen.</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Initial account/password</dt>
<dd>
<p>admin / !admin1234</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_1_manager_dashboard.png" alt="3 1 1 manager dashboard">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 4. LENA initial screen (DASHBOARD)</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_node_installation_command_line"><a class="link" href="#_node_installation_command_line">3.1.2. Node Installation (Command Line)</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Installing a Node is the same as extracting the LENA installation package. On the servers where you will install WAS and the Web Server, upload the respective installation packages to a prepared path (e.g., /engn001/lena or /engn001/lenaw) and extract them.<br>
After installing the Node, scripts to start, stop, and check the status of the Node Agent are available as shown below.</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<caption class="title">Table 7. Node Agent management scripts</caption>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-center valign-top">Script Path</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-center valign-top">Script Name</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-center valign-top">Remarks</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-center valign-middle" rowspan="3"><p class="tableblock">Under the Node installation path 'bin'<br>
(e.g., /engn001/lena/1.3/bin)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-center valign-top"><p class="tableblock">start-agent.sh</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">Run Node Agent</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-center valign-top"><p class="tableblock">ps-agent.sh</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">Check Node Agent process</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-center valign-top"><p class="tableblock">stop-agent.sh</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">Stop Node Agent</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_was_node_installation"><a class="link" href="#_was_node_installation">WAS Node Installation</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Consider the following when installing a WAS Node:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Install LENA Manager and WAS Node on the same server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install LENA Manager and WAS Node on different servers (standalone LENA Manager)</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In case 1, the WAS Node is already installed because the WAS Node installation package was extracted to install LENA Manager in <a href="#_lena_manager_installationexecution">LENA Manager Installation/Execution</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In case 2, upload the LENA WAS installation package to the prepared path (e.g., /engn001/lena) on the server where the WAS Node will be installed, and extract it as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="title">Verify installation path and uploaded file</div>
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash"> [lena]# cd /engn001/lena
 [lena]# ll
 -rw-rw-r-- 1 lena lena lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock tip">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-tip" title="Tip"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When extracting, a directory is created using the filename excluding the extension.<br>
Rename this directory to the simplified name 1.3 and use it.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="title">Extract installation file / Rename directory</div>
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash"> [lena]# tar -xvzf lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz
 [lena]# mv lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0 1.3
 [lena]# ll
 drwxr-xr-x 12 lena lena 1.3
 -rw-rw-r-- 1 lena lena lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After installing the Node, run the Node Agent with start-agent.sh.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="title">Run Node Agent</div>
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">[lena]# cd /engn001/lena/1.3/bin
[lena]# ./start-agent.sh
Input JAVA_HOME path for LENA. ( q: quit )
JAVA_HOME PATH :
/engn001/java/jdk1.8.0_202 <i class="conum" data-value="1"></i><b>(1)</b>
Input Agent port for LENA Agent. ( q: quit )
Agent port (Default : 16800):
16800 <i class="conum" data-value="2"></i><b>(2)</b>
Input Agent user for LENA Agent. ( q: quit )
Agent user (Default : lena):
lena <i class="conum" data-value="3"></i><b>(3)</b>

--------------------------------
 LENA Agent
--------------------------------
Using LENA_HOME : /engn001/lena/1.3
Using JAVA_HOME : /engn001/java/jdk1.8.0_202/jre
Using CONF_FILE : /engn001/lena/1.3/conf/agent.conf
Using LOG_HOME : /engn001/lena/1.3/logs/lena-agent
Using RUN_USER : lena
Using PORT : 16800
Using UUID : 98449860-0a9a-323b-9766-98c4292000df
LENA Agent is started.</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The input items when running Node Agent are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="colist arabic">
<table>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="1"></i><b>1</b></td>
<td>Enter JAVA HOME (jdk) path</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="2"></i><b>2</b></td>
<td>Enter the port Node Agent will use</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="3"></i><b>3</b></td>
<td>Enter the OS account to run Node Agent</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_was_node_installation_when_changing_spec"><a class="link" href="#_was_node_installation_when_changing_spec">WAS Node Installation (when changing spec)</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The procedure to change the WAS Node spec is as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Perform WAS Node installation with the base installation file.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Before proceeding with additional server installation, perform a depot change.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>LENA_HOME/bin/change-depot.sh <path-to-depot-file></p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">[lena]$ ./change-depot.sh ~/lena-depot-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0-EN9.tar.gz
*******************************
* LENA Depot Change ! *
*******************************
========================= Execution Result ========================
RESULT : Success
MESSAGE : depot change succeeded from EN8 to EN9
===================================================================

Execution is completed.!!</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The naming rule for the depot file is as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>lena-depot-{os name}-{lena version}-{engine number}</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Example) lena-depot-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0-EN9.tar.gz</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_web_server_node_installation"><a class="link" href="#_web_server_node_installation">Web Server Node Installation</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Upload the LENA Web Server installation package to the server where the Web Server will be installed and extract it.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="title">Verify path / file</div>
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash"> [lenaw]# cd /engn001/lenaw
 [lenaw]# ll
 -rw-rw-r-- 1 lena lena lena-web-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="title">Extract installation file / Rename directory</div>
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash"> [lenaw]# tar -xvzf lena-web-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz
 [lenaw]# mv lena-web-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0 1.3
 [lenaw]# ll
 drwxr-xr-x 12 lena lena 1.3
 -rw-rw-r-- 1 lena lena lena-web-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When extracting, a directory is created using the filename excluding the extension.<br>
Rename this directory to the simplified name 1.3 and use it.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After installing the Node, run the Node Agent with start-agent.sh.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="title">Run Node Agent</div>
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">[lena]# cd /engn001/lenaw/1.3/bin
[lena]# ./start-agent.sh
Input JAVA_HOME path for LENA. ( q: quit )
JAVA_HOME PATH :
/engn001/java/jdk1.8.0_202 <i class="conum" data-value="1"></i><b>(1)</b>
Input Agent port for LENA Agent. ( q: quit )
Agent port (Default : 16900):
16900 <i class="conum" data-value="2"></i><b>(2)</b>
Input Agent user for LENA Agent. ( q: quit )
Agent user (Default : lena):
lena <i class="conum" data-value="3"></i><b>(3)</b>
Input Web Agent Engine type for LENA Agent. ( q: quit )
Agent Engine type [EN-A, EN-N] (Default : EN-A):
EN-A <i class="conum" data-value="4"></i><b>(4)</b>
Openssl version 1.1.1 detected.
Input your openssl version(1.0.1, 1.0.2, 1.1.1 or 3.0) (Default : 1.1.1, q:quit):
1.1.1 <i class="conum" data-value="5"></i><b>(5)</b>
Do you want to select the module for the openssl version 1.1.1? Make sure all of your instances are shut down(Y/N, Default:Y)
Y <i class="conum" data-value="6"></i><b>(6)</b>

The modules have been copied successfully.
--------------------------------
 LENA Agent
--------------------------------
Using LENA_HOME : /engn001/lenaw/1.3
Using JAVA_HOME : /engn001/java/jdk1.8.0_202/jre
Using CONF_FILE : /engn001/lena/1.3/conf/agent.conf
Using LOG_HOME : /engn001/lena/1.3/logs/lena-agent
Using RUN_USER : lena
Using PORT : 16900
Using UUID : 98449860-0a9a-323b-9766-98c4292000df
LENA Agent is started.</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The input items when running Node Agent are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="colist arabic">
<table>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="1"></i><b>1</b></td>
<td>Enter JAVA HOME (jdk) path</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="2"></i><b>2</b></td>
<td>Enter the port Node Agent will use</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="3"></i><b>3</b></td>
<td>Enter the OS account to run Node Agent</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="4"></i><b>4</b></td>
<td>Enter the Web Server Engine Type that Node Agent will use
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Default : EN-A</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Engine Type : EN-A (legacy Apache-based), EN-N (Nginx-based)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The engine type is decided at the first Agent startup; cross-engine (EN-A, EN-N) usage is not allowed within a single Agent</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="5"></i><b>5</b></td>
<td>Enter OpenSSL version</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><i class="conum" data-value="6"></i><b>6</b></td>
<td>Confirm OpenSSL version selection</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_integration_registration_of_lena_manager_and_nodes"><a class="link" href="#_integration_registration_of_lena_manager_and_nodes">Integration (Registration) of LENA Manager and Nodes</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After installing WAS Node and Web Server Node and starting the Agent, you can register Nodes through LENA Manager.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Click the 'SERVER' menu at the top of LENA Manager to check the Node List.<br>
Click the 'Register' button to register a Node; an empty row is added as shown below, and fill in each input item.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_2_node_register_01.png" alt="3 1 2 node register 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 5. SERVER menu initial screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The items to input when registering a Node are as follows:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Node Name: Name of the Node to register</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node Type: Select either Application / Web</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node IP: IP Address of the server where the Node is installed</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node Port: Node Port entered at Node installation</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For Manager Address, the IP of the server where LENA Manager is installed is auto-filled, so no separate input is needed.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After entering all items, click the 'Save' button to complete Node registration; if successful, you will see a screen like the following.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can check the engine type via the Engine field.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>EN-A : Apache-based Web Server Engine</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>EN-N : Nginx-based Web Server Engine</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_2_node_register_02.png" alt="3 1 2 node register 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 6. Example of successful Node registration</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_remote_node_installation_lena_manager_web_ui"><a class="link" href="#_remote_node_installation_lena_manager_web_ui">3.1.3. Remote Node Installation (LENA Manager Web UI)</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In addition to the method described in <a href="#_node_installation_command_line">Node Installation (Command Line)</a>, Nodes can also be installed remotely through LENA Manager.
To do this, upload the LENA installation files (WAS, Web Server) into a specific directory on the server where LENA (Manager) is installed.
An example of the path where you should upload the installation packages:</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<caption class="title">Table 8. Installation file upload path for remote installation (example)</caption>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-center valign-top">LENA Installation Path</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-center valign-top">LENA installation package upload path</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-center valign-top"><p class="tableblock">/engn001/lena/1.3 (LENA_HOME)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-center valign-top"><p class="tableblock">[LENA_HOME]/repository/install-files/default</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Upload the WAS and Web Server installation packages you used earlier to that path.</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="title">Verifying installation packages for remote installation</div>
<div class="content">
<pre class="CodeRay highlight"><code data-lang="bash">[lena]# cd /engn001/lena/1.3/repository/install-files/default
[lena]# ll
-rw-rw-r--. 1 lena lena lena-enterprise-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz
-rw-rw-r--. 1 lena lena lena-web-linux_na_x86_64-1.3.3.0.tar.gz</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If you have uploaded the installation packages to the appropriate path, select the 'SERVER' menu on LENA Manager and click the 'Install' button at the bottom.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_3_node_install_remote_01.png" alt="3 1 3 node install remote 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 7. Example of remote WAS Node installation</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The items that must be entered for remote Node installation are as follows:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Node Type: Select either Application / Web</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node Name: Name of the Node to install on the remote server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node Address: IP Address of the remote server where the Node will be installed</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node Port: Port that the Node will use on the remote server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>User: OS account of the remote server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Password: Password of the OS account of the remote server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>SSH Port: SSH Port of the remote server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>LENA Home: Path where the Node will be installed on the remote server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Java Home: Installed JAVA Home path on the remote server</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Based on the values entered for remote installation, LENA Manager transfers the pre-prepared installation package files to the remote server, installs the Node, and automatically starts the Agent of the installed Node, completing the remote installation. You can check the progress in a popup window.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_3_node_install_remote_02.png" alt="3 1 3 node install remote 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 8. Example of checking progress of remote WAS Node installation</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When installation completes successfully, the remotely installed Node is automatically registered in LENA Manager.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_3_node_install_remote_03.png" alt="3 1 3 node install remote 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 9. Example after remote Node installation and registration completion</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock warning">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-warning" title="Warning"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For remote Node installation, the SSH Port firewall must be open between the server where LENA Manager is installed and the server where the remote installation will be performed.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_was_installationexecution"><a class="link" href="#_was_installationexecution">3.1.4. WAS Installation/Execution</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After installing and registering the WAS Node, you can now install WAS through the LENA Manager Web UI.
Click the 'SERVER' menu at the top of LENA Manager, then select the WAS Node on the left where you want to install WAS to view the WAS List. Click the 'Install' button on this screen.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_4_was_install_01.png" alt="3 1 4 was install 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 10. Viewing WAS List</div>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_4_was_install_02.png" alt="3 1 4 was install 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 11. WAS installation popup and example inputs</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Clicking the 'Install' button opens a popup to enter information for installing WAS, and the input items are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Server Type: Type of WAS, choose between Standard / Enterprise</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node: Node where WAS will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Server ID: Name for LENA Manager to identify the WAS</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Service Port: The base HTTP Port upon which WAS installation is configured</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Run User: OS account used to start WAS (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install Root Path: Path where WAS will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Log Home: Path for WAS logs</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>default: [Install Root Path]/logs</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>custom: user-defined path</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>JVM Route: Value for the Web Server to identify WAS when integrated with Web Server</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>auto: automatically generated by LENA</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>manual: user-defined</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When WAS starts, it uses various ports such as HTTP, HTTPS, and AJP. For convenience during WAS installation in LENA, only the HTTP Port is entered, and other port values are automatically calculated and installed based on it.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After entering all WAS installation information, click the 'Save' button to install WAS, and you can check the installed WAS in the WAS List.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_4_was_install_03.png" alt="3 1 4 was install 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 12. WAS List after normal WAS installation</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To start a stopped WAS, click the 'Start' button on the right of the WAS List. To stop a running WAS, the 'Stop' button appears in the same location; click that button.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When starting WAS, the WAS startup log (and Application startup log if an application is deployed) is displayed in a popup.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_4_was_install_04.png" alt="3 1 4 was install 04">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 13. WAS startup and logs</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_weba_server_installationexecution"><a class="link" href="#_weba_server_installationexecution">3.1.5. WebA Server Installation/Execution</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the same way as WAS installation, you can install the Web Server through the LENA Manager Web UI. Select a Web Server Node with engine EN-A, and you can install WebA Server.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_5_weba_install_01.png" alt="3 1 5 weba install 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 14. Viewing Web Server List</div>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_5_weba_install_02.png" alt="3 1 5 weba install 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 15. Web Server installation popup and example inputs</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Clicking the 'Install' button opens a popup to enter information for installing the Web Server, and the input items are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Server Type: Web Server (fixed)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node: Node where the Web Server will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Server ID: Name for LENA Manager to identify the Web Server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Service Port: HTTP Port the Web Server will use</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Run User: OS account used to start the Web Server (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Web Server Engine Path: Engine path to be used when installing the Web Server (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install Root Path: Path where the Web Server will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Log Home: Path for Web Server logs</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>default: [Install Root Path]/logs</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>custom: user-defined path</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When the Web Server starts, it uses various ports such as HTTP and HTTPS. For Web Servers of the EN-N engine type, only the base port is entered during installation, and installation is performed for that type based on it. Adding other types later is possible, but the initially installed base type cannot be deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After entering all Web Server installation information, click the 'Save' button to install the Web Server. You can check it in the Web Server List.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_5_weba_install_03.png" alt="3 1 5 weba install 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 16. Web Server List after normal installation</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To start a stopped Web Server, click the 'Start' button on the right of the Web Server List. To stop a running Web Server, the 'Stop' button appears in the same location; click that button.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When starting the Web Server, the Web Server startup log is displayed in a popup.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_5_weba_install_04.png" alt="3 1 5 weba install 04">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 17. Web Server startup and logs</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_weba_server_was_integration"><a class="link" href="#_weba_server_was_integration">3.1.6. WebA Server - WAS Integration</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This section explains the integration settings between WebA Server and WAS. The integration between WebA Server and WAS can be configured on the Web Server settings screen.
From the 'SERVER' menu at the top of LENA Manager, select the installed Web Server to open the settings screen, and select the 'Connector' tab at the top of the settings screen.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_6_weba_was_connect_01.png" alt="3 1 6 weba was connect 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 18. Initial Web Server settings screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>On the Web Server’s 'Connector' tab, you manage the connection settings between the Web Server and WAS.<br>
Adding the WAS to be integrated in the Load Balancer Worker List at the bottom of the 'Connector' tab completes the basic integration between the Web Server and WAS.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To add the WAS to be integrated, click the 'Add Worker' button on the Configuration tab of the Load Balancer section; in the popup, select the installed WAS and click 'Save'.<br>
In the popup, you can check the WAS list per WAS Node registered in LENA Manager, and WAS already registered in 'Connector' are not shown.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_6_weba_was_connect_02.png" alt="3 1 6 weba was connect 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 19. Adding WAS to integrate</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once the WAS to be integrated is added to the WAS List, click the 'Save' button at the bottom right to save the list.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_6_weba_was_connect_03.png" alt="3 1 6 weba was connect 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 20. Saving the list of WAS to integrate</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_webn_server_installationexecution"><a class="link" href="#_webn_server_installationexecution">3.1.7. WebN Server Installation/Execution</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As with WebA Server installation, you can install a Web Server through the LENA Manager Web UI. Select a Web Server Node with engine EN-N, and you can install WebN Server.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_7_webn_install_01.png" alt="3 1 7 webn install 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 21. Viewing Web Server List</div>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_7_webn_install_02.png" alt="3 1 7 webn install 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 22. Web Server installation popup and example inputs</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Clicking the 'Install' button opens a popup to enter information for installing the Web Server, and the input items are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Node: Node where the Web Server will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Server ID: Name for LENA Manager to identify the Web Server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Service Port: Port Type and Port Number the Web Server will use</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>Port Type : There are four types of Port Type; the default type determined at installation cannot be changed. (Port Number can be edited.)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>HTTP : HTTP protocol-based Web Server (can be started immediately after installation)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>HTTPS : HTTPS protocol-based Web Server (requires adding an SSL certificate after installation to start)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>TCP : Net Gateway based on TCP port (can be started immediately after installation)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>UDP : Net Gateway based on UDP port (can be started immediately after installation)</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Run User: OS account used to start the Web Server (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Web Server Engine Path: Engine path to be used when installing the Web Server (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install Root Path: Path where the Web Server will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Log Home: Path for Web Server logs</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>default: [Install Root Path]/logs</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>custom: user-defined path</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When the Web Server starts, it uses various ports such as HTTP and HTTPS. For Web Servers of the EN-N engine type, only the base port is entered during installation, and installation is performed for that type based on it. Adding other types later is possible, but the initially installed base type cannot be deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After entering all Web Server installation information, click the 'Save' button to install the Web Server. You can check it in the Web Server List.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_7_webn_install_03.png" alt="3 1 7 webn install 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 23. Web Server List after normal installation</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To start a stopped Web Server, click the 'Start' button on the right of the Web Server List. To stop a running Web Server, the 'Stop' button appears in the same location; click that button.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When starting the Web Server, the Web Server startup log is displayed in a popup.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_7_webn_install_04.png" alt="3 1 7 webn install 04">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 24. Web Server startup and logs</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_webn_server_was_integration_proxy"><a class="link" href="#_webn_server_was_integration_proxy">3.1.8. WebN Server - WAS Integration (Proxy)</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This section explains the integration settings between WebN Server and WAS. The integration between WebN Server and WAS can be configured on the WebN Server settings screen.
From the 'SERVER' menu at the top of LENA Manager, select the installed WebN Server to open the settings screen, and select the 'Connector' tab at the top of the settings screen.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_8_webn_was_proxy_connect_01.png" alt="3 1 8 webn was proxy connect 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 25. Initial Web Server settings screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>On the WebN Server 'Connector' tab, you manage the connection settings between WebN Server and WAS.
Adding the WAS to be integrated in the Load Balancer > Configuration tab > Load Balancer Member List under the 'Connector' tab > Proxy tab completes the basic integration between WebN Server and WAS.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To add the WAS to be integrated, click the 'Add Member' button on the Configuration tab of the Load Balancer section; in the popup, select the installed WAS and click 'Save'.
In the popup, you can check the WAS list per WAS Node registered in LENA Manager, and WAS already registered in 'Connector' are not shown.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_8_webn_was_proxy_connect_02.png" alt="3 1 8 webn was proxy connect 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 26. Adding WAS to integrate</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once the WAS to be integrated is added to the WAS List, click the 'Save' button at the bottom right to save the list.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_8_webn_was_proxy_connect_03.png" alt="3 1 8 webn was proxy connect 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 27. Saving the list of WAS to integrate</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_webn_server_was_integration_net_gateway"><a class="link" href="#_webn_server_was_integration_net_gateway">3.1.9. WebN Server - WAS Integration (Net Gateway)</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This section explains the integration settings between WebN Server and Backend Server. The integration between WebN Server and Backend Server can be configured on the WebN Server settings screen.
From the 'SERVER' menu at the top of LENA Manager, select the installed WebN Server to open the settings screen, and select the 'Connector' tab at the top of the settings screen. Then select the 'Net Gateway' tab below.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_9_web_was_net_connect_01.png" alt="3 1 9 web was net connect 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 28. Initial Web Server settings screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>On the 'Net Gateway' tab under the WebN Server 'Connector' tab, you manage the connection settings between WebN Server and Backend Server.
Adding the Backend Server to be integrated in the Load Balancer Worker List at the bottom of the 'Connector' tab completes the basic integration between Web Server and Backend Server.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To add a Backend Server to integrate, click the 'Add Upstream' button on the Configuration tab of the Load Balancer section; in the list that opens, directly enter the IP or DNS and Port, and click 'Save'.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_9_web_was_net_connect_02.png" alt="3 1 9 web was net connect 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 29. Adding Backend Server to integrate</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Once the Backend Server to be integrated is added to the Member List, click the 'Save' button at the bottom right to save the list.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_9_web_was_net_connect_03.png" alt="3 1 9 web was net connect 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 30. Saving the list of Backend Servers to integrate</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_session_server_installation_and_integration"><a class="link" href="#_session_server_installation_and_integration">3.1.10. Session Server Installation and Integration</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Install the Session Server when applying Session Clustering; it can be installed in the following two ways.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Standalone mode: Install Session Server on a separate server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Embedded mode: Do not install Session Server on a separate server; install it in embedded form within an already installed WAS</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_standalone_mode_installation_and_was_integration"><a class="link" href="#_standalone_mode_installation_and_was_integration">Standalone Mode Installation and WAS Integration</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Session Server can be installed on a WAS Node. Select the 'SERVER' menu at the top of LENA Manager and select the WAS Node where you will install the Session Server.
At the bottom of the WAS List, you can check the Session Server List where the installed Session Servers can be viewed.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_10_session_install_01.png" alt="3 1 10 session install 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 31. Viewing Session Server List</div>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_10_session_install_02.png" alt="3 1 10 session install 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 32. Session Server installation popup and example inputs</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Clicking the 'Install' button opens a popup to enter information for installing the Session Server, and the input items are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Server Type: Standalone (fixed)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Node: Node where the Session Server will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Server ID: Name for LENA Manager to identify the Session Server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Service Port: Port that the Session Server will use</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Mirror Server IP: Node where the other Session Server is installed (choose from registered Nodes)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Mirror Server Port: Port used by the Session Server on the Node where the other Session Server is installed</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Run User: OS account used to start the Session Server (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install Root Path: Path where the Session Server will be installed (not editable)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Log Home: Path for Session Server logs</p>
<div class="olist loweralpha">
<ol class="loweralpha" type="a">
<li>
<p>default: [Install Root Path]/logs</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter manually: user-defined path</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After entering all Session Server installation information, click the 'Save' button to install the Session Server; you can check it in the Session Server List.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In a Session Clustering configuration, install two Session Servers and configure redundancy with one as Primary and the other as Secondary.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the example above, another WAS Node is specified for 'Mirror Server IP'; install a Session Server on that WAS Node as well as below.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_10_session_install_03.png" alt="3 1 10 session install 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 33. Installing the other Session Server</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After installing all Session Servers, select the 'Session' tab on the WAS settings screen to integrate with WAS.<br>
The 'Session' tab manages the settings required to apply Session Clustering for WAS by integrating with Session Servers. Change the 'Session Clustering Enable' item to 'Yes' to display detailed settings. In Standalone Mode, Session Servers are installed separately and integrated with WAS to apply Session Clustering.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_10_session_install_04.png" alt="3 1 10 session install 04">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 34. WAS Standalone mode Session Server settings</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Based on the Standalone mode Session Server, the settings are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Primary Server Host: Select the Node where the Session Server designated as Primary is installed, and select the Session Server.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Secondary Server Host: Select the Node where the Session Server designated as Secondary is installed, and select the Session Server. When two Session Servers are installed, after selecting the Primary Server Host, the remaining Session Server is automatically designated as Secondary.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>External Stored Session: Along with applying Session Clustering, select whether to manage Session information on the two Session Servers only (instead of WAS and two Session Servers). This option is commonly used when configured on Cloud or Container environments. (Default false)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Share session in applications: If multiple applications are deployed to WAS, select whether to share Session information among the applications. (Default false)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Multi Login Control: Select whether to enable the duplicate login control feature. (Default false)</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For Standalone mode Session Servers, you must apply the above settings for each WAS to which the configuration applies.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After changing Session settings, the WAS must be restarted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_embedded_mode_installation_and_was_integration"><a class="link" href="#_embedded_mode_installation_and_was_integration">Embedded Mode Installation and WAS Integration</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Select the WAS on which you will use the Session Server function in Embedded mode, open the settings screen, and select the 'Session' tab at the top.<br>
The 'Session' tab manages the settings required to apply Session Clustering for WAS by integrating with Session Server. Change the 'Session Clustering Enable' item to 'Yes' to display detailed settings. In Embedded Mode, the Session Server function is embedded in WAS and runs within WAS.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_10_session_install_05.png" alt="3 1 10 session install 05">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 35. WAS Embedded mode Session Server settings</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Based on the Embedded mode Session Server, the settings are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Embedded Host: When Embedded Mode is selected, it is fixed to the current WAS.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Embedded Port: Enter the port used by the Embedded Session Server.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Secondary Server Host: Specify the WAS on which to use the other Embedded Session Server. Select the Node where WAS is installed, then select WAS.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Secondary Server Port: Enter the port used by the other Embedded Session Server.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Multi Login Contorl: Select whether to enable the duplicate login control feature. (Default false)</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After finishing entering and selecting the settings, click the 'Save' button to complete the Embedded Session settings. When the Embedded Session settings are completed on one WAS, the settings are also applied to the other WAS.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After changing Session settings, the WAS must be restarted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_10_session_install_06.png" alt="3 1 10 session install 06">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 36. Completion of WAS Embedded mode Session Server settings</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_verifying_inter_server_integration"><a class="link" href="#_verifying_inter_server_integration">3.1.11. Verifying Inter-Server Integration</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This section explains how to verify the integration settings performed through the processes described in <a href="#_weba_server_was_integration">WebA Server - WAS Integration</a>, <a href="#_webn_server_was_integration_proxy">WebN Server - WAS Integration (Proxy)</a>, <a href="#_webn_server_was_integration_net_gateway">WebN Server - WAS Integration (Net Gateway)</a>, and <a href="#_session_server_installation_and_integration">Session Server Installation and Integration</a>.<br>
LENA Manager provides a Topology View for easily checking the configuration of installed servers. Using this Topology feature, you can verify whether integration is normal, and you can also verify integration using the LENA Sample pages that come preloaded during Web Server and WAS installation.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_verification_via_topology"><a class="link" href="#_verification_via_topology">Verification via Topology</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Click the 'Topology' menu at the top of LENA Manager.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_11_check_connect_01.png" alt="3 1 11 check connect 01">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 37. Topology View</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the Topology View, you can basically check the currently registered Nodes, the configuration of Servers installed per Node, and the integration information.<br>
In the figure above, two Web Servers, two WAS, and two Session Servers are installed, and the integration settings between Web Server and WAS, and between WAS and Session Server are represented with connecting lines, through which you can verify that the inter-server integration has been performed correctly.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_verification_via_sample_page"><a class="link" href="#_verification_via_sample_page">Verification via Sample Page</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>LENA’s Web Server and WAS come with a default Sample Page and Sample Application. These can also be used to verify proper integration after initial installation.<br></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>First, check the Web Server’s IP and Port, then enter the following in a web browser.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>http://[Web Server IP]:[Web Server Port]/index.html</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You will see that the index.html page provided by LENA is called as shown below, and you can verify that the Web Server is called successfully.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_11_check_connect_02.png" alt="3 1 11 check connect 02">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 38. Web Server call test</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_verification_via_sample_application"><a class="link" href="#_verification_via_sample_application">Verification via Sample Application</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you install LENA WAS, the default application provided by LENA is loaded. By calling index.jsp and session.jsp of this application, you can test WAS calls and Session Clustering respectively.<br></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Assuming that the Web Server and WAS are in their initial installed state, enter the following in a web browser.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>http://[Web Server IP]:[Web Server Port]/index.jsp</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the Web Server and WAS are connected normally, the request called with the Web Server IP and Port is forwarded to the WAS, which then requests the index.jsp page, and the index.jsp page provided by the LENA Sample Application is called as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_11_check_connect_03.png" alt="3 1 11 check connect 03">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 39. index.jsp call test</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you call the index.jsp page, you can check which WAS is handling the current request via the Server ID, Service Port, and JvmRout values.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Next, call session.jsp with the same Web Server IP and Port as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>http://[Web Server IP]:[Web Server Port]/session.jsp</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you call session.jsp, additional Session information about the current request is displayed. As you repeat the calls, the Session Count increases, and from the second call, the issued Session ID is displayed.
To verify that Session Clustering has been applied correctly, after a Session ID is issued, stop the WAS currently handling the request, then refresh the web browser to send the request again.
Even though another running WAS handles the request, the Session ID remains the same and the Session Count increases, which confirms correct clustering.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/installation/vmhost/3_1_11_check_connect_04.png" alt="3 1 11 check connect 04">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 40. session.jsp call test</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="footer">
<div id="footer-text">
Version 1.3.3.0<br>
Last updated 2025-09-21 08:28:03 +0900
</div>
</div>
</body>
</html></div>
