</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_snapshot"><a class="link" href="#_snapshot">Snapshot</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you click the Snapshot button in the Overview tab, a window for creating a Snapshot appears; click Save to create a Server Cluster Snapshot.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Snapshots can be created only when the Server Cluster is in a synchronized state.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Snapshot tab provides a screen to manage the list of Snapshots. Enter a date to query Snapshot history. You can view details of Snapshot history and restore to a desired point in time.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Click the <span class="button">list button</span> in the Detail column of the Snapshot list to view details for that snapshot.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Snapshot information is managed per server, so servers added to the Cluster after a particular Snapshot was created are excluded from restoration to that Snapshot.
(In this case, after restoring the Snapshot, perform Sync again so that all servers have the same configuration.) Also, if a specific server is deleted from the Cluster after a Snapshot, all Snapshot information for that server is deleted. When creating a Snapshot, source code is not copied to the Snapshot; the copied configuration files include only basic configuration files, application configuration files, and enterprise.xml.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Creating Snapshots can put a load on disk capacity, so create with care. Also, created Snapshots are not deleted automatically; the user must delete them manually. Therefore, we recommend deleting unnecessary Snapshots at an appropriate time.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect1">
<h2 id="_resource"><a class="link" href="#_resource">6. Resource</a></h2>
<div class="sectionbody">
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_database"><a class="link" href="#_database">6.1. Database</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you select Database from the left menu, the Database Resource list is displayed.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_database.png" alt="resource database">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 10. Database List Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_database_registration"><a class="link" href="#_database_registration">6.1.1. Database Registration</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">New button</span> in the Database Resource list to display the new registration screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the input fields.</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Enter the Resource Name.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Check the DriverClassName and select the driver for your desired vendor.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the Address (host/Port) information.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_database_modification"><a class="link" href="#_database_modification">6.1.2. Database Modification</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the checkbox of the Database Resource you want to modify from the Database Resource list.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Modify the Database Resource items and save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When content is modified, it propagates to the DataSource Resource and WAS configuration connected to that Database Resource, so if there are DataSource Resources connected under that Database Resource, the input fields are disabled by default.
Click the <span class="button">Edit button</span> to enable modification.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_datasource"><a class="link" href="#_datasource">6.2. DataSource</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you select DataSource from the left menu, the DataSource Resource list is displayed.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_datasource.png" alt="resource datasource">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 11. DataSource List Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_datasource_registration"><a class="link" href="#_datasource_registration">6.2.1. DataSource Registration</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">New button</span> in the DataSource Resource list to display the new registration screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter a logical name in the Resource Name field.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Set the Server Type. Server Type must be selected from Standard or Enterprise, and thereafter it can only be imported and used on servers of the same type.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the detailed settings for DataSource (refer to the detailed item descriptions in <a href="#Server DataSource Settings">[Server DataSource Settings]</a>)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Upload button</span> to register the Driver for that DataSource on the Manager server. Pre-registered Drivers are transmitted to the corresponding server when operators import them to the server.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>JDBC Drivers uploaded to the Manager are transmitted to the corresponding server when operators import that DataSource Resource to the server.
Transmitted JDBC Drivers are located in the {server home path}/lib/datasource directory and are automatically registered in the Classpath.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_datasource_modification"><a class="link" href="#_datasource_modification">6.2.2. DataSource Modification</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>When you select a row you want to modify from the DataSource Resource list, the DataSource Resource modification screen is displayed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Change the configuration you want to modify.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_datasource_detail.png" alt="resource datasource detail">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 12. DataSource Detail Information Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you save after modifying DataSource Resource information, the changed configuration propagates to the server where that DataSource Resource is used.
When you restart the server where the configuration has propagated, that configuration is applied.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After importing a DataSource Resource set to Standard Type to a Standard server, the Server Type cannot be changed to Enterprise.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Note that when deleting a DataSource Resource after Classpath registration, the Classpath is not deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_datasource_deletion"><a class="link" href="#_datasource_deletion">6.2.3. DataSource Deletion</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the checkbox of the DataSource Resource you want to delete from the DataSource Resource list.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Delete button</span> to delete.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If there are Registered Servers or Registered Applications that have imported from the Server or Application, that DataSource Resource cannot be deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jdbc_driver_upload"><a class="link" href="#_jdbc_driver_upload">6.2.4. JDBC Driver Upload</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Upload button</span> in the DataSource Resource registration or edit screen to display a screen where you can upload Driver Files.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">File Selection button</span> to select the Driver File you want to upload from your local PC.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Upload button</span> to upload the Driver File to the Manager.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_datasource_import"><a class="link" href="#_datasource_import">6.2.5. DataSource Import</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The list of Servers using the created DataSource Resource by importing it (when Scope is Context, Global, Global + Link) or the list of Applications (when Scope is Application) is displayed in the lower area when viewing DataSource Resource details.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_datasource_from_datasource_detail_screen"><a class="link" href="#_importing_datasource_from_datasource_detail_screen">Importing DataSource from DataSource Detail Screen</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>DataSource Resources with Scope Context, Global, or Global + Link can register servers that import them.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>In the DataSource management screen, select a specific DataSource Resource to navigate to the detail information screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Edit Server List button</span> to display a window where you can register and manage servers.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Specify the server to import that DataSource and move it to the right area.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to import the DataSource Resource to that server.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To delete an imported DataSource Resource from a server, move the target server to the left area and click the <span class="button">Save button</span>.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_datasource_from_individual_server"><a class="link" href="#_importing_datasource_from_individual_server">Importing DataSource from Individual Server</a></h5>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the Servers menu from the top of LENA Manager.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click on the left side: Individual Web Application Server > Resources > DataSource tab to display a screen where you can view the DataSource Resource list for that server and add DataSource Resources.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Import button</span> to display a list of predefined DataSource Resources in a popup window.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the DataSource Resource you want to import.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">OK button</span> to import that DataSource Resource.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you import a DataSource Resource, connection information between that DataSource Resource and the server is internally created.
Based on this connection information, configuration updates are delivered to that server when the DataSource Resource is modified.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Standard Servers cannot import Enterprise Type DataSource Resources. (They are not displayed in the list)</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Imported DataSource Resource settings cannot be edited in Server settings. (Configuration information can be viewed but not modified)
To change the configuration, go to the Resource > DataSource screen to make changes.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_jta"><a class="link" href="#_jta">6.3. JTA</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you select JTA from the left menu, the JTA Resource list is displayed.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_jta.png" alt="resource jta">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 13. JTA List Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jta_registration"><a class="link" href="#_jta_registration">6.3.1. JTA Registration</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">New button</span> in the JTA list to display the new registration screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the values you want to configure. (For detailed settings, refer to "4.3.7 Server Configuration Information Management")</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jta_modification"><a class="link" href="#_jta_modification">6.3.2. JTA Modification</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>When you select a row you want to modify from the JTA Resource list, the modification screen is displayed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the configuration you want to change.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_jta_detail.png" alt="resource jta detail">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 14. JTA Detail Information Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you save after modifying JTA Resource information, the changed configuration propagates to the server where that JTA Resource is used. When you restart the server where the configuration has propagated, that configuration is applied.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jta_deletion"><a class="link" href="#_jta_deletion">6.3.3. JTA Deletion</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the checkbox of the JTA Resource you want to delete from the JTA list.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Delete button</span> to delete.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If there are Registered Servers that have imported from the server, that JTA Resource cannot be deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jta_import"><a class="link" href="#_jta_import">6.3.4. JTA Import</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The list of servers using the created JTA Resource by importing it is displayed in the lower area when viewing JTA Resource details.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_jta_from_jta_detail_screen"><a class="link" href="#_importing_jta_from_jta_detail_screen">Importing JTA from JTA Detail Screen</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the JTA detail screen, you can modify the list of servers that are importing and using it.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>In the JTA management screen, select a specific JTA Resource to navigate to the detail information screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Edit Server List button</span> to display a window where you can register and manage servers.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Specify the server to import that JTA Resource and move it to the right area.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to import the JTA Resource to that server.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To delete an imported JTA Resource from a server, move the target server to the left area and click the <span class="button">Save button</span>.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_jta_from_individual_server"><a class="link" href="#_importing_jta_from_individual_server">Importing JTA from Individual Server</a></h5>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the Servers menu from the top of LENA Manager.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click on the left side: Individual Web Application Server > Resources > JTA tab to display a screen where you can view the JTA Resource list for that server and add JTA Resources.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Import button</span> to display a list of predefined JTA Resources in a popup window.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the JTA Resource you want to import.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">OK button</span> to import that JTA Resource.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you import a JTA Resource, connection information between that JTA Resource and the server is internally created.
Based on this connection information, configuration updates are delivered to that server when the JTA Resource is modified.
Connection information can be viewed in the Resource > JTA screen.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Imported JTA Resource settings cannot be edited in server settings. (Configuration information can be viewed but not modified)
To change the configuration, go to the Resource > JTA screen to make changes.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_jms"><a class="link" href="#_jms">6.4. JMS</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you select JMS from the left menu, the JMS Resource list is displayed.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_jms.png" alt="resource jms">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 15. JMS List Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jms_registration"><a class="link" href="#_jms_registration">6.4.1. JMS Registration</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">New button</span> in the JMS list to display the new registration screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>When you select the type of JMS Resource to register, configuration information appropriate for the selected type is displayed below.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the values you want to configure. (For detailed settings, refer to "4.3.7 Server Configuration Information Management")</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jms_modification"><a class="link" href="#_jms_modification">6.4.2. JMS Modification</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>When you select a row you want to modify from the JMS Resource list, the modification screen is displayed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the configuration you want to change.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_jms_detail.png" alt="resource jms detail">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 16. JMS Detail Information Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you save after modifying JMS Resource information, the changed configuration propagates to the server where that JMS Resource is used. When you restart the server where the configuration has propagated, that configuration is applied.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jms_deletion"><a class="link" href="#_jms_deletion">6.4.3. JMS Deletion</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the checkbox of the JMS Resource you want to delete from the JMS list.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Delete button</span> to delete.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If there are Registered Servers that have imported from the server, that JMS Resource cannot be deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_jms_import"><a class="link" href="#_jms_import">6.4.4. JMS Import</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The list of servers using the created JMS Resource by importing it is displayed in the lower area when viewing JMS Resource details.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_jms_from_jms_detail_screen"><a class="link" href="#_importing_jms_from_jms_detail_screen">Importing JMS from JMS Detail Screen</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the JMS detail screen, you can modify the list of servers that are importing and using it.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>In the JMS management screen, select a specific JMS Resource to navigate to the detail information screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Edit Server List button</span> to display a window where you can register and manage servers.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Specify the server to import that JMS and move it to the right area.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to import the JMS Resource to that server.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To delete an imported JMS Resource from a server, move the target server to the left area and click the <span class="button">Save button</span>.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_jms_from_individual_server"><a class="link" href="#_importing_jms_from_individual_server">Importing JMS from Individual Server</a></h5>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the Servers menu from the top of LENA Manager.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click on the left side: Individual Web Application Server > Resources > JMS tab to display a screen where you can view the JMS Resource list for that server and add JMS Resources.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Import button</span> to display a list of predefined JMS Resources in a popup window.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the JMS Resource you want to import.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">OK button</span> to import that JMS Resource.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you import a JMS Resource, connection information between that JMS Resource and the server is internally created.
Based on this connection information, configuration updates are delivered to that server when the JMS Resource is modified.
Connection information can be viewed in the Resource > JMS screen.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Imported JMS Resource settings cannot be edited in server settings. (Configuration information can be viewed but not modified)
To change the configuration, go to the Resource > JMS screen to make changes.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_application"><a class="link" href="#_application">6.5. Application</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you select Application from the left menu, the Application Resource list is displayed.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_application.png" alt="resource application">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 17. Application List Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_application_registration"><a class="link" href="#_application_registration">6.5.1. Application Registration</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">New button</span> in the Application list to display the new registration screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the values you want to configure.</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>If Application Type is WAR, additional configurable items are displayed. (For detailed settings, refer to <a href="#WAS_Application_Settings">Application Settings</a>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_application_modification"><a class="link" href="#_application_modification">6.5.2. Application Modification</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>When you select a row you want to modify from the Application Resource list, the modification screen is displayed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Enter the configuration you want to change.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to save.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/resource_application_detail.png" alt="resource application detail">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 18. Application Detail Information Screen</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you save after modifying Application Resource information, the changed configuration propagates to the Server where that Resource is used.
The Server where the configuration has propagated will apply that configuration when restarted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_application_deletion"><a class="link" href="#_application_deletion">6.5.3. Application Deletion</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the checkbox of the Application Resource you want to delete from the Application list.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Delete button</span> to delete.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If there are Registered Servers that have imported from the Server, that Application Resource cannot be deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_application_upload"><a class="link" href="#_application_upload">6.5.4. Application Upload</a></h4>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Upload button</span> in the Application Resource registration or edit screen to display a screen where you can upload Application Files.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">File Selection button</span> to select the Application File you want to upload from your local PC.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Upload button</span> to upload the Application File to the Manager.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_application_import"><a class="link" href="#_application_import">Application Import</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The list of Servers that are using the created Application Resource by importing it is displayed in the lower area of the Application Resource detail view.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_application_from_application_detail_screen"><a class="link" href="#_importing_application_from_application_detail_screen">Importing Application from Application Detail Screen</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the Application detail screen, you can modify the list of Servers that are importing and using it.</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>In the Application management screen, select a specific Application Resource to navigate to the detail information screen.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Edit Server List button</span> to display a window where you can register and manage Servers.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Specify the Server to import that Application and move it to the right area.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Save button</span> to import the Application Resource to that Server.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>To delete an imported Application Resource from a Server, move the target Server to the left area and click the <span class="button">Save button</span>.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_importing_application_from_individual_server"><a class="link" href="#_importing_application_from_individual_server">Importing Application from Individual Server</a></h5>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p>Select the Servers menu from the top of LENA Manager.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click on the left side: Individual Web Application Server > Applications menu to display a screen where you can view the Application Resource list for that Server and add Application Resources.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">Import button</span> to display a list of predefined Application Resources in a popup window.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select the Application Resource you want to import.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click the <span class="button">OK button</span> to import that Application Resource.</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you import an Application Resource, connection information between that Application Resource and the Server is internally created.
Based on this connection information, configuration updates are delivered to that Server when the Application Resource is modified.
Connection information can be viewed in the Resource > Application screen.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Imported Application Resource settings cannot be edited in Server settings. (Configuration information can be viewed but not modified)
To change the configuration, go to the Resource > Application screen to make changes.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect1">
<h2 id="_diagnostics"><a class="link" href="#_diagnostics">7. Diagnostics</a></h2>
<div class="sectionbody">
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_monitoring_dashboard"><a class="link" href="#_monitoring_dashboard">7.1. Monitoring Dashboard</a></h3>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_status_summary"><a class="link" href="#_status_summary">7.1.1. Status Summary</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Monitoring Dashboard provides three tabs at the bottom, and the summary information shown at the top changes depending on the selected tab.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Information by tab is as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="dlist">
<dl>
<dt class="hdlist1">Node tab </dt>
<dd>
<p>Provides server monitoring information by registered Node</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Server Cluster tab </dt>
<dd>
<p>Provides server monitoring information by Server Cluster group</p>
</dd>
<dt class="hdlist1">Service Cluster tab </dt>
<dd>
<p>Provides container monitoring information by Service Cluster group</p>
</dd>
</dl>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can set the refresh interval for each view. For WAS, click the <span class="button">popup button</span> in the Function column to move to the detailed monitoring view.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Monitoring Dashboard screens are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_monitoring_dashboard_node_tab.png" alt="diagnostics monitoring dashboard node tab">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 19. Monitoring Dashboard - Node tab</div>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_monitoring_dashboard_cluster_tab.png" alt="diagnostics monitoring dashboard cluster tab">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 20. Monitoring Dashboard - Server Cluster tab</div>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/container/monitoring_serviceCluster.png" alt="monitoring serviceCluster">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 21. Monitoring Dashboard - Service Cluster tab</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock important">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-important" title="Important"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Service Cluster tab is available in the Container Edition.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The properties used in the Monitoring Dashboard are as follows. For utilization values, you can change the color thresholds using the Status Range property. (See the Monitoring Settings subsection in this chapter.)</p>

</div>
<div class="title">Figure 22. Dump window</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can generate and download Heap Dump, Thread Dump, and Active Service Dump.
In general, dumps are created to investigate root causes when errors such as Out Of Memory, excessive Thread Pool usage, or service delays occur on a server.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Depending on the dump type you want to generate, click <span class="button">Thread Dump button</span>, <span class="button">Active Service Dump button</span>, or <span class="button">Heap Dump button</span> to create the dump.
Generated dumps are stored on the Host where the Web Application Server runs:
Thread Dump at {log_home}/logs/tdump, Active Service Dump at {log_home}/logs/sdump, and Heap Dump at {log_home}/logs/hdump.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Click the <span class="button">Delete button</span> to delete dump files.
Click the <span class="button">Download button</span> to download dump files. When downloading, the dump file is downloaded as a zip along with the system status dump file.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">

<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_detailed_status_monitoring"><a class="link" href="#_detailed_status_monitoring">7.1.2. Detailed Status Monitoring</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the Monitoring Dashboard, select the <span class="button">middle button (View Detail Chart)</span> in the Function column to monitor detailed Thread, Memory, and service information.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_system_tab"><a class="link" href="#_system_tab">System tab</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can check the Web Application Server’s Memory, Thread, and Service information.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_current_status_system.png" alt="diagnostics current status system">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 23. System tab</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="_memory_chart"><a class="link" href="#_memory_chart">Memory Chart</a></h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Real-time memory usage is displayed.
The provided metrics are GC Time (time spent in Garbage Collection), GC Count, Heap Used (Total Memory - Free Memory),
and Total Memory (total memory used by the server).
The red dashed line on the chart indicates the maximum available Heap Memory. Therefore, pay attention if Heap Memory usage stays near the red dashed line for a long time without a normal GC pattern.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The maximum number of Request Threads can be changed from the Server menu via the maxThreads property of the Web Application Server.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="_thread_chart"><a class="link" href="#_thread_chart">Thread Chart</a></h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This line chart shows the usage of Request Threads that the Web Application Server manages as a pool to handle user requests.
The red dashed line indicates the maximum number of Request Threads available. Pay attention if the number of Request Threads approaches the red dashed line.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The maximum number of Request Threads can be changed from the Server menu via the maxThreads property of the Web Application Server.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="_thread_list"><a class="link" href="#_thread_list">Thread List</a></h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can view all Threads in the Web Application Server.
You can filter by the printed Thread name or Thread state.
The Thread List fields are as follows.</p>

<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_datasource_tab"><a class="link" href="#_datasource_tab">DataSource tab</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can view the DataSource information configured on the Application Server.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_current_status_datasource.png" alt="diagnostics current status datasource">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 24. DataSource tab</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="_datasource_chart"><a class="link" href="#_datasource_chart">DataSource Chart</a></h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The numbers of Active Connections and Idle Connections are displayed on the chart in real time.
The red dashed line indicates the configured maximum number of connections.
Be careful when Active Connections approach the red dashed line.
Use the combo box to select and monitor other DataSources.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The maximum number of connections can be changed via the maxConnection property on the DataSource registration screen.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect5">
<h6 id="_datasource_information"><a class="link" href="#_datasource_information">DataSource Information</a></h6>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can check the configuration information for the selected DataSource.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_monitoring_settings"><a class="link" href="#_monitoring_settings">7.1.3. Monitoring Settings</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can set basic monitoring configurations in DIAGNOSTICS > Policy > Common Rule Setting.
The settings are as follows.</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<caption class="title">Table 129. Monitoring-related default settings</caption>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Field</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Default</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Status Range</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Configure thresholds for Resource Low, Middle, and High in the Monitoring Dashboard.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Low if below 60%, Middle if 60% or above, High if 80% or above</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Diagnostics Interval</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Set the diagnostics interval.</p></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Dump Limit</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Per-server dump count limit for each dump directory (Thread/ActiveService/Heap). 0 means unlimited.</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">200 (files)</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_analysis_dashboard"><a class="link" href="#_analysis_dashboard">7.2. Analysis Dashboard</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Analysis Dashboard provides real-time failure analysis information at the system level.
The provided information types are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Performance Map</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Analysis Summary</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Instance Map</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_analysis_dashboard.png" alt="diagnostics analysis dashboard">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 25. Analysis Dashboard</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_performance_map"><a class="link" href="#_performance_map">7.2.1. Performance Map</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Performance Map in the top-left of the Analysis Dashboard provides system state information based on each of "Thread & Elapsed", "Thread", and "Elapsed".
Each system is represented as a colored circle on the chart. The colors by system state are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Normal: Green</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Anomaly: Orange (An anomaly situation was detected by diagnostics)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Fault: Red (A fault situation was detected by diagnostics)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The meanings of the X and Y axes in the chart are as follows.</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<caption class="title">Table 130. Meanings of the X and Y axes in the Performance Map chart</caption>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>

<div class="paragraph">
<p>Displays the summary information of the number of diagnostic results currently detected, the total number of diagnostic results that occurred today, and the total number of diagnostic results that occurred on the previous day (Default: 1 day ago).</p>
</div>

<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_instance_map"><a class="link" href="#_instance_map">7.2.3. Instance Map</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When you select a specific system in the Performance Map, you can view a Time Line Chart showing server information and diagnostic results within the system at the bottom of the screen.
Servers are displayed in different colors depending on their status, and you can toggle specific servers to show/hide them in the Time Line Chart on the right.
When Anomaly or Fault situations are detected after diagnostics, they are displayed in orange (Anomaly) or red (Fault) on the Time Line; double-click the area to view the Report.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_event_dashboard"><a class="link" href="#_event_dashboard">7.3. Event Dashboard</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Event Dashboard provides information on events that occurred in WAS.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Event information is generated in WAS and delivered to Manager via UDP.
Events sent by WAS are stored in the Manager DB for a certain period (3 months),
while detailed SQL and Exception Trace information for those events is stored for 7 days only due to their large data size.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_event_types"><a class="link" href="#_event_types">7.3.1. Event Types</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>There are four types of events as follows:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Out Of Memory Error event in WAS</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Full GC event in WAS</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Stuck Thread event in WAS</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Exception event in WAS</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>WAS Exception events are generated and sent to Manager in the following two cases:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>When an Exception is thrown outside the service method of a Servlet for a user request</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>When an Exception of a type configured by the user occurs</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_managing_events_via_the_event_dashboard"><a class="link" href="#_managing_events_via_the_event_dashboard">7.3.2. Managing Events via the Event Dashboard</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can manage collected events in the Event Dashboard of LENA Manager.</p>
</div>

</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can check the trend of event occurrences by date using a bar chart.
You can view all Systems or specify a particular System or Server to query.
Click the <span class="button">calendar button</span> to change the date.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The Event list fields are as follows.</p>

<div class="paragraph">
<p>Click an individual event row to view the Event details as shown below.</p>

<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_statistics"><a class="link" href="#_statistics">7.4. Statistics</a></h3>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_yearly_diagnosticsaction_statistics"><a class="link" href="#_yearly_diagnosticsaction_statistics">7.4.1. Yearly Diagnostics/Action Statistics</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>From DIAGNOSTICS > Analysis > Diagnostics Trend, yearly diagnostic results per server are provided via charts.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_statistics.png" alt="diagnostics statistics">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 30. Statistics screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>On this screen you can check the following:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Diagnostics Calendar</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Each cell represents a day. When you mouse over a date in the yearly statistics chart, you can see how many diagnostics occurred on that date.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Daily Diagnostics Detail</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>When you click a specific date in the Diagnostics Calendar, a graph showing the number of diagnostics by hour for the selected date is displayed at the bottom of the screen.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_report"><a class="link" href="#_report">7.4.2. Report</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When diagnostics and actions run, a Report is automatically generated.
Reports are retained for 7 days, and older Reports are automatically deleted.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_diagnosticsaction_report_list"><a class="link" href="#_diagnosticsaction_report_list">Diagnostics/Action Report List</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In DAIGNOSTICS > Analysis > Diagnostics Trend, after selecting a specific server, click the <span class="button">Report List button</span> to see the Diagnostics/Action Report list screen.
The list screen looks as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_report_list.png" alt="diagnostics report list">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 31. Diagnostics/Action Report list screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can click the <span class="button">View button</span> to open a Report.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_common_information_in_report"><a class="link" href="#_common_information_in_report">Common Information in Report</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>While the Report contents vary depending on the diagnostic results, they share the following common information.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_report.png" alt="diagnostics report">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 32. Diagnostics/Action Report screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>It visualizes the causal relationships among diagnostic results detected during the period when the abnormal symptom persisted,
and at the bottom of the screen shows the time slots when each diagnostic result was generated.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An Anomaly indicates that only part of the conditions configured in the Diagnostics/Action Rule were met and is displayed in orange,
whereas a Fault indicates that all conditions configured in the Diagnostics/Action Rule were met and is displayed in red.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect4">
<h5 id="_report_details"><a class="link" href="#_report_details">Report Details</a></h5>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>From the Time Line at the bottom of the Report, click a specific diagnostic type at a specific time to view details as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_report_detail.png" alt="diagnostics report detail">

<h4 id="_notifications"><a class="link" href="#_notifications">7.4.3. Notifications</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When a Report is generated via diagnostics/actions, you can check it via the <span class="icon">bell icon</span> at the top-right of LENA Manager.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_alert.png" alt="diagnostics alert">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 34. Diagnostics/Action result notification</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Selecting a notification opens the generated Report immediately. If you want to acknowledge and hide it, click the <span class="button">x button</span>.
If there are many notifications, click the <span class="icon">bell icon</span> at the top-right of Manager to open the Notifications screen and review them in bulk.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_alert_list.png" alt="diagnostics alert list">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 35. Bulk acknowledgement of Diagnostics/Action result notifications</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Clicking the <span class="icon">Home icon</span> navigates to the diagnostics history screen for the selected notification.
Clicking the <span class="icon">V icon</span> marks the selected notification as acknowledged; acknowledged notifications no longer appear in the <span class="icon">bell icon</span> list at the top-right.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>In the Notifications screen you can review notifications from within the last month. Data older than one month is automatically deleted.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>

<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_diagnostics_and_actions"><a class="link" href="#_diagnostics_and_actions">7.5. Diagnostics and Actions</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By using Diagnostics and Actions, you can proactively diagnose potential failures and automatically perform appropriate actions to improve server stability.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>The diagnostics feature automatically determines the possibility of server failure (or a failure state) based on rules.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The action feature helps maintain stable service by automatically performing appropriate server controls based on diagnostic results to withstand failure situations.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The target diagnostic types are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Excessive use of the Request Pool (Request Full)</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>When service requests are excessive and all available Request Threads on the server are exhausted, service requests may be delayed or result in an unavailable state.
Based on Request Thread usage, determine whether service requests are excessive,
and automatically redirect such requests to a temporary page to keep the server stable.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Bulk DB Data Request</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>When a service processes large amounts of DB data, it may consume excessive memory, leading to OOM, frequent Full GCs, and server hang.
Determine whether a service is making bulk DB data requests,
and forcibly terminate the service to keep the server stable.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Excessive use of the DB Connection Pool (DB Conn Full)</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>When DB connections are overly occupied due to DB processing delays, WAS-DB network latency, or DB locks,
services are delayed until they can obtain an available DB connection.
If services waiting for DB connection allocation accumulate and overly occupy the Request Thread Pool, it may lead to service unavailability.
When all DB connections in a specific DataSource are exhausted, shorten the allocation wait time to isolate the failure and keep the server stable.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Long-running services (Long Transaction)</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>If services are delayed due to transient network or inter-system issues, or if there are inherently long-running services,
those services can excessively occupy available Request Threads, hindering other services.
Limit Request Thread usage for long-running services to guarantee QoS for other services.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Server hang (Hang)</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>When the server enters a hang state where it cannot operate, not only are all tasks stopped, but it may also affect the entire system where the server is installed.
When a hang is detected, restart immediately to resolve the server failure and prevent system-wide failures.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>Out of Memory error (OOM)</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>OOM errors can occur due to service logic errors or excessive memory usage.
Because normal server operation cannot be guaranteed when OOM occurs, quickly detect OOM and automatically restart to overcome the server failure.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<p>User surge (Peak Control)</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>When the number of user requests exceeds server capacity, services may be delayed or unavailable.
If user requests concentrate on a specific service, control requests to enter sequentially to provide stable service while preventing user churn.
This also guarantees QoS for other services.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="sect3">

<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The relationships among Hang diagnostic settings are as follows:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Fault condition: If, due to a server hang, there is no response for Timeout(s) after attempting a Health Check and this repeats for Retry Count times, it is considered a Fault and an Action is performed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Anomaly condition: If the number of Full GCs within FullGC Duration(s) reaches FullGC Count, it is considered an Anomaly and only a Warning report is generated without any Action.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_server_rule_setting"><a class="link" href="#_server_rule_setting">7.5.2. Server Rule Setting</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>From DIAGNOSTICS > Policy > Server Rule Setting, you can map Diagnostics/Action Rules to servers and enable/disable them.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Initially, no diagnostic Rules are mapped. Before you can enable/disable Rules, you must first map Diagnostics/Action Rules.
Click the row for each server to map Diagnostics/Action Rules to the server as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_current_status_server_rule_mapping.png" alt="diagnostics current status server rule mapping">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 44. Diagnostics Rule Mapping screen</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>After Rules are mapped, you can enable/disable them from the Server Rule Setting screen as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="imageblock">
<div class="content">
<img src="https://docs.lenalab.org/resources/1.3.4.2/static/images/manual/diagnostics_current_status_server_rule_setting.png" alt="diagnostics current status server rule setting">
</div>
<div class="title">Figure 45. Server Rule Setting screen</div>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Only the Peak Control diagnostic Rule is configured from DIAGNOSTICS > Policy > Peak Control Rule Setting.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_trace"><a class="link" href="#_trace">7.6. Trace</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Trace records the movement path and time of the corresponding request across LENA Servers for failure diagnosis so that the cause can be identified.
The Trace types provided by LENA are as follows.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Session Trace</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Event Trace</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can access various functions from the submenus under DIAGNOSTICS > Trace.</p>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_session_id_search"><a class="link" href="#_session_id_search">7.6.1. Session ID Search</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can check the Session Trace information (which server holds the session).
To search for a session, the clustered Session Server must be running.</p>
</div>

</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Trace information is retained for one week only.

<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">WAS</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">WAS that processed the request</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Event</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Event that occurred</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">JVMRoute</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">JVMRoute value of the WAS that processed the request</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">SESSION ID</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">SESSION ID of the request</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session Server</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session Server that processed the request</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Labeled as the Primary/Secondary Session Server connected to the WAS</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">URL</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">URL of the request</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The traceable events are as follows (you can see the event codes in log files; the screen shows descriptive sentences instead of codes).</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<caption class="title">Table 162. Traceable event codes and descriptions</caption>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 25%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Event Code</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Note</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">sywz</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session ID and JVMRoute information differ. (Can occur when failover happens due to a WAS failure.)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session ID does not match with JVMRoute.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">wxso</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">No session information in WAS but session information exists in the Session Server. (Can occur when failover happens due to a WAS failure.)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session does not exist in Application Server.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">wosx</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session information exists in WAS but not in the Session Server. (Can occur if both Session Servers were restarted.)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session does not exist in Session Server.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">wxsx</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">No session information in both WAS and Session Server. (Can occur if both Session Servers are stopped.)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session does not exist in any Server.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">woxx</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session information exists in WAS, but the connection to both Primary & Secondary Session Servers is lost. (Can occur if both Session Servers are stopped.)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session Server does not respond.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">wxxx</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">No session information in WAS and the connection to both Primary & Secondary Session Servers is lost. (Can occur if the session timed out in WAS and both Session Servers are stopped.)</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Session Server does not respond.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="admonitionblock note">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-note" title="Note"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the sywz and wxso events occur repeatedly for a single request, both events are shown in one search result.</p>
</div>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
</div>

<div class="sect2">
<h3 id="_tuna_apm"><a class="link" href="#_tuna_apm">7.7. TunA APM</a></h3>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>TunA APM provides an easy way to integrate LENA with the TunA APM tool so you can conveniently monitor the performance of your application.
As of LENA 1.3.2, it is available on Linux/Unix OS and VM installation versions.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>You can configure the integration and environment from the submenus under DIAGNOSTICS > TunA APM.
The TunA APM menu consists of the following:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Connection Management</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Module Management</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install Management</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Host Management</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="sect3">
<h4 id="_connection_management"><a class="link" href="#_connection_management">7.7.1. Connection Management</a></h4>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Manage the IP Address and Port information for the TunA collector server and the Web Server.<br>
Based on the IP Address and Port entered by the user, a test is performed to check if a connection to the TunA collector server is possible.</p>
</div>
